-- lean/Unfalsifiable.lean — GENERATED. UNFALSIFIABILITY — the algebra of a claim no evidence can move, and the exactly-one verdict the non-justiciable record reaches. Seals why uuidna can neither prove nor refute an allegation about the world: with no decidable test and no sealed citation the trial returns NOT PROVEN, always. HONEST SCOPE: this wing decides the SHAPE of claims (does evidence do any work?), never the truth of any actual allegation; it adjudicates nothing and names no one. UNVERIFIED means "not decidable here", never "false". Every proof `by decide`, sorry-free, no Mathlib, and axiom-free — depends on NO axiom beyond the leanprover/lean4 kernel (verified by scripts/lean-axioms; not even propext).

-- the verdict model of Legal.lean, restated so this wing verifies standalone: t = a decidable test exists,
-- h = the test holds, c = the claim cites a sealed authority.
def up (t h c : Nat) : Nat := t*h + c - t*h*c                    -- PROVEN
def ur (t h c : Nat) : Nat := t * (1 - h) * (1 - c)              -- REFUTED
def unp (t h c : Nat) : Nat := (1 - up t h c) * (1 - ur t h c)   -- NOT PROVEN

-- THE CONSPIRACY RECORD HAS EXACTLY ONE REACHABLE VERDICT. A conspiracy claim is the record (t=0, c=0): no decidable test exists, and it cites no sealed theorem. For every h, unp 0 h 0 = 1 — NOT PROVEN, always. It is the whole answer to "can the coins explain any conspiracy": they cannot, because with no test and no citation the trial has one door and it is not an explanation.
theorem untested_uncited_is_not_proven : (List.range 2).all (fun h => unp 0 h 0 == 1) := by decide

-- THE COINS MINT NO EXPLANATION. With no decidable test (t=0), PROVEN reduces to the citation alone: up 0 h c = c, for every h. So nothing about the coins, the trial, or the ledger can carry a claim to PROVEN — only a sealed authority can, and an allegation about the world has none. This is why "the coins explain any conspiracy" is refused by the ledger rather than by an opinion.
theorem no_test_no_proof_without_citation : (List.range 2).all (fun h => (List.range 2).all (fun c => up 0 h c == c)) := by decide

-- NOT PROVEN IS NOT A FINDING OF FALSEHOOD — the two verdicts never coincide on the non-justiciable record: for every h and c, unp 0 h c + ur 0 h c ≤ 1 and ur 0 h c = 0. A UNVERIFIED stamp on an undecidable claim says the ledger cannot decide it, never that it is false. Publishing such a verdict as evidence about the world inverts its meaning.
theorem not_proven_is_not_refuted : (List.range 2).all (fun h => (List.range 2).all (fun c => ur 0 h c == 0 && unp 0 h c + ur 0 h c <= 1)) := by decide

-- THE SIGNATURE OF UNFALSIFIABILITY, DECIDED. A claim confirmed by the evidence AND by its absence is a claim the evidence never touched: ((e → c) ∧ (¬e → c)) = c on every assignment. The evidence variable drops out of the expression entirely — that is what "no evidence could change my mind" means as algebra, and it is checkable in four rows.
theorem absorbed_evidence_does_no_work : ([true, false].all (fun e => [true, false].all (fun c => ((!e || c) && (e || c)) == c))) = true := by decide

-- A CLAIM THAT FORBIDS NOTHING SAYS NOTHING. Information is what a claim EXCLUDES: over the four (e,c) rows, the always-true claim rules out 0 of them, while a falsifiable one (here e → c) rules out exactly 1. Zero exclusions is zero content — the unfalsifiable claim and the empty claim are the same object, measured.
theorem unfalsifiable_excludes_nothing : ((List.range 4).filter (fun n => !true)).length == 0 && ((List.range 4).filter (fun n => !(!(n%2 == 1) || (n/2 == 1)))).length == 1 := by decide
